scenes.headline: Agents & subagents: plan, build, ship
scenes.sub: Delegate like a lead, not a typist.
lines: Lesson seven. Agents and subagents.
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
This is where you stop typing, and start leading.

after: With subagents, you can hand the work to a whole team of them.

scenes.headline: Split big work across specialists.
lines: One agent doing everything gets slow, and confused.
Instead, hand pieces to specialists. One researches, one builds, one reviews.
Each works in its own clean context, so the main thread stays sharp.

scenes.headline: Role. Tools. Instructions.
lines: An agent is another markdown file.
It has a role, and a list of tools it may use.
Then its instructions. This reviewer can read, but never edit.
scenes.code:
---
name: reviewer
description: Reviews diffs for bugs.
  Use after every edit.
tools: Read, Grep, Bash
---
You are a strict code reviewer.
Report bugs by severity.
Never edit files.

scenes.headline: A brief that works.
lines: Delegating well means writing a good brief.
The goal, and why it matters.
What done looks like.
What not to touch.
And what to report back.

cards.d: What to hand you at the end

scenes.headline: Plan. Build. Test. Ship.
lines: Put it together.
Approve the plan.
Let agents build in parallel.
Have the reviewer, and the tests, check the work.
Then push to git, and deploy.

scenes.headline: What you just learned.
lines: Quick recap.
You lead. Specialist agents build, each in a clean context. You review.
Your mission: create one reviewer agent, and run it after your next change.
